Human-verified witness comparison

Tetrastichon on Saint Anne

A four-line pilot collated directly from three digitized editions of De laudibus sanctissimae matris Annae. The display separates what the witnesses print from normalization and from OCR behavior.

OCR is not variation. This pilot finds no substantive verbal variation in the four lines. OCR output is retained only as a diagnostic record and is never promoted to the textual apparatus.

The witnesses

Read each column independently. The restrained ribbons simply keep corresponding verse lines in view; they carry no claim about descent or dependence.

Collation and classification

Every classified textual variation unit; readings link back to their witness facsimiles.
Line / classLemmaM1494L1497L1501Editorial note
2 · punctuationmeritis et meritis. etmeritis . etmeritis.et All witnesses print a point after meritis; only spacing differs. The normalized layer removes the medial point.
4 · orthographicplacidam placidāplacidamplacidam M1494 abbreviates final -m with a macron; the Leipzig witnesses spell the ending out.
2 · punctuationpotens. potens.potenspotens M1494 closes the line with a point; no terminal point is visible in the Leipzig witnesses.
3 · punctuationveneratur. veneratur.veneraturveneratur M1494 closes the line with a point; no terminal point is visible in the Leipzig witnesses.
4 · punctuationopem. opem.opemopem M1494 closes the tetrastich with a point; no terminal point is visible in the Leipzig witnesses.

OCR audit trail

These disagreements were checked against the scans and excluded from the apparatus. They describe machine recognition, not the transmitted text.

  • L1497: OCR anns → verified anna. The scan clearly prints anna.
  • L1497: OCR Memo → verified Nemo. The scan clearly prints Nemo.
  • L1501: OCR auna → verified anna. The scan clearly prints anna.
  • L1501: OCR Memo → verified Nemo. The scan clearly prints Nemo.

Editorial record and downloads

human-verified-from-facsimile, 2026-07-26. All four lines in all three witnesses were read directly from the linked BSB scans.

Diplomatic text preserves printed spelling, abbreviation marks, capitalization, and sentence punctuation while representing long s as s. Normalized text expands abbreviation marks and supplies consistent punctuation; it does not modernize vocabulary.
